chunk_map.heading: How we work in this room

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Walked all 10 chunks for pronoun/demonstrative/definite-NP referents. Chunk 0 line 3's 'M1' resolves via the renderer's own persistent chrome, not a body-internal referent: rule 11's own text confirms 'the deck derives section codes (M1.../P/S.../R...)' shown in the nav rail for every slide of this file, so a reader is never without that label. Chunk 7 Key Concepts' './CLAUDE.local.md' and 'The loop is orient -> fix -> close -> compound' both resolve against chunk 3's What You'll Learn bullets ('Compound the session into a personal rules file at ./CLAUDE.local.md'; 'Run an orient -> fix -> close -> compound loop'). Chunk 8's 'AE101 from here on' is defined in the same sentence it's used. Chunk 9's 'Your rules file' resolves against chunk 3/7's established ./CLAUDE.local.md; 'that session' resolves against 'Module 2', named earlier in the same sentence. Chunk 8's forward reference to 'Module 2' is the module file's own legitimate cross-module sequencing (check_lectures.md rule 3 assigns exactly this job to module files, not lecture bodies -- this file IS the module file). Harm check: rule 1 exists to stop a slide the reader cannot follow because a term points nowhere; no such gap found in any chunk, so no REVISE.

No chunk points at another file by position. Chunk 8's four Pre-reads entries each name their source in the link text or the surrounding sentence (Willison; Horthy/HumanLayer; Cherny; the multi-session guide) -- none is located as 'the lecture that opened...'. The eight lecture/exercise links in chunk 6 (Start here) are structural include-links, out of scope per rule 13's own text. 'Cherny calls parallel worktrees his single biggest productivity unlock' (chunk 8) names Cherny and his video in the same bullet that introduced them, not by position.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is M1, the training's first module: no prior in-training exercise/lecture beat exists for the body to reference backward against, and the body attempts none. Chunk 2's 'the repo you picked' describes the module's own Prework flow (pick a repo, then open the first session in it), not a 'the X you did/saw' pointer at a beat inside the module's exercise/lecture set -- it is the Prework section describing what Prework covers, not a backward reference to it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body. This file is module scaffolding (Big Idea, Prework, LOs, room norms, autonomy, entry links, recap, pre-reads, bridge), not a live-demo beat -- those live in the linked exercises/lectures, out of this file's scope.

All 9 named chunks carry multi-sentence or multi-bullet, self-carrying content; the shortest, chunk 1 Big Idea at 22 words / two sentences, is still a complete standalone claim, and chunk 9 Next at 34 words / two sentences matches the file's own Next-closer convention. None is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

Every header is literally true of its own chunk: Big Idea states the idea; Prework describes prework; What You'll Learn lists five Bloom-verb LOs; How we work in this room states room norms; Freedom to choose states room autonomy/pacing; Start here opens with the trick-share question then the module's entry links; Key Concepts recaps five taught points; Pre-reads before Module 2 is literally a reading list for the gap before M2; Next states what M2 does and what carries forward. No chunk's content contradicts its own header.

Checked each sub-item per chunk: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction (chunk 3's 'no plan mode' is one clause in a five-item list, not the banned triadic-negation shape); no anaphora/epistrophe triples (chunk 4's three bolded room-norm leads and chunk 5's five Freedom-to-choose bullets each use distinct, non-repeated lead words); no self-grading superlatives ('Cherny calls parallel worktrees his single biggest productivity unlock', chunk 8, is Cherny's own attributed claim about his practice, not the training grading its own worth -- same carve-out shape as external-authority praise elsewhere in the corpus); no number-plus-retraction anywhere in body; no abstraction-noun stacks; no verb triplets with an empty leg.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget -- bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 3's five What-You'll-Learn bullets (bolded verbs Run/Distinguish/Fix/Close/Compound) and chunk 8's four Read:/Watch: mode labels both match rule 9's own named exceptions verbatim (module-shape.md's bolded-verb LO template, and the 2026-08-13 reading-list/menu waiver for mode-word-only bold) -- N/A by construction, no accept-note owed, confirmed the bold spans are exactly the template-mandated word ('Read:', 'Watch:', one verb each) with titles left plain. Chunk 4's three room-norm bullets ('**All learners.**', '**Exercises.**', '**Share and discuss.**') are the exact pattern rule 9 itself names as 'genuinely open, not covered here' (no template mandates this section's shape). Each bold span is 1-3 words functioning as a checklist-item-style handle, well inside the <=5-word cap -- the banned monoculture shape is 'every bullet opens with a bolded SENTENCE', and these are short labels, not sentences. Harm check: no comprehension or trust cost found from three short room-norm handles on a room-agreement slide; the budget's purpose (stop a wall of bold from reading as noise) isn't triggered by three 1-2-word tags. Checked `pre-cohort-todos.md` and this file's own maintainer block for an existing accept-note on this exact pattern -- none exists (unlike an earlier instance of this judgment, no standing maintainer TODO is actually on record for it). Not filing a REVISE per the harm-absent path; flagging as an open rule question instead, matching what check_slides.md itself already says is unresolved.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: If the maintainer wants this settled rather than left open: extend rule 9's exception list to name short (<=3-word) checklist-style room-norm labels as handles, the way it already names LO verbs and Read:/Watch: mode words -- or state explicitly that per-bullet bold on ground-rule lists is the monoculture violation regardless of span length.
